tickerText: [TENNIS] Wimbledon 2026 Sunday, July 12: Linda Noskova is the women's champion after a dramatic 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 win over Karolina Muchova in the first all-Czech final — the 21-year-old survived five squandered championship points before converting on her sixth to become the youngest Wimbledon winner since Petra Kvitova in 2011 • Centre Court's men's final pits defending champion Jannik Sinner against Roland Garros winner Alexander Zverev at 4 p.m. BST — Sinner leads their rivalry 10-4 and rides a 13-match Wimbledon streak after dismantling Novak Djokovic in the semis • [SQUASH] The PSA tour turns to Tasmania with the Eastside Open in Hobart, July 22–26 at Eastside Squash Centre — PSA Satellite registration closes July 17 ahead of first matches July 24, followed by the Victorian Open in Melbourne July 29–Aug 2 • [BADMINTON] The DAIHATSU Japan Open Super 750 opens Tuesday July 14 at Tokyo Metropolitan Gymnasium with a $950,000 purse — Indonesia sends 12 players led by fourth seed Jonatan Christie, Malaysia's Leong Jun Hao faces Taiwan's Chi Yu-jen in men's singles, and Soh Wooi Yik and Man Wei Chong debut their new men's doubles partnership • [PICKLEBALL] The PPA Australia 250 Melbourne runs July 16–19 at Raya Pickleball Club and Pickle4Real with 407 players registered, then Singapore hosts its inaugural Leapmotor PPA Asia 500 Open July 23–26 at The Sports Arina @ Expo — 658 players entered and weekend championship-court tickets are sold out for the $70,000 pro draw • [TABLE TENNIS] WTT Star Contender São José dos Campos 2026 enters its third ticket release July 12 ahead of the July 21–26 event at Vale Sul Shopping — the first Star Contender in São Paulo state features world No. 5 Hugo Calderano and Bruna Takahashi among 80-plus international players competing for a $300,000 purse

newsItems.title: Noskova Survives Five Match Points to Win Wimbledon Title
newsItems.excerpt: Linda Noskova claimed her first Grand Slam title with a 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 victory over fellow Czech Karolina Muchova in Saturday's historic all-Czech Wimbledon final. The 21-year-old squandered five championship points while leading 5-2 in the second set before regrouping to become the youngest Wimbledon champion since Petra Kvitova in 2011. Sunday's men's final pits defending champion Jannik Sinner against Alexander Zverev at 4 p.m. BST on Centre Court.

newsItems.title: PSA Tour Shifts to Hobart as Eastside Open Registration Closes
newsItems.excerpt: The professional squash calendar moves to Tasmania for the Eastside Open, July 22–26 at Eastside Squash Centre in Hobart. PSA Satellite registration closes July 17, with first matches July 24, alongside local singles and doubles brackets. The tour then heads to the Victorian Open in Melbourne, July 29–Aug 2.

newsItems.title: Japan Open Super 750 Opens Tuesday With Full Regional Squads
newsItems.excerpt: The DAIHATSU Japan Open begins July 14 at Tokyo Metropolitan Gymnasium with a $950,000 purse. Indonesia fields 12 players including fourth seed Jonatan Christie, while Malaysia's Leong Jun Hao opens against Taiwan's Chi Yu-jen in men's singles. Soh Wooi Yik and Man Wei Chong debut their new men's doubles partnership, and Pearly Tan and Thinaah Murugesan lead the women's doubles draw.

newsItems.title: WTT Star Contender Brazil Enters Final Ticket Release
newsItems.excerpt: The third batch of tickets for WTT Star Contender São José dos Campos 2026 goes on sale July 12 ahead of the July 21–26 event at Vale Sul Shopping. The first Star Contender in São Paulo state will feature world No. 5 Hugo Calderano and Bruna Takahashi among 80-plus international players competing across singles, doubles and mixed doubles for a $300,000 purse.
